# OL Analytics API — Architecture & Data Flows

_Generated 2026-10-14 15:27 UTC · c4gen dev_

ol-analytics-api is a multi-tenant, read-only FastAPI gateway over StarRocks. Each consumer is a tenant: an independent FastAPI sub-app with its own routes, auth model and OpenAPI document, mounted on one root app that owns the shared StarRocks connection pool, Vault credential refresh, health checks and observability. Two tenants were mounted as of October 2026. `b2b_dashboard` (/api/v1/analytics) serves k-anonymized B2B site-license aggregates (contract utilization, enrollment funnel, engagement trend, program funnel, content engagement, needs-attention) plus a consent-gated learner-progress view (the consent gate fails open in QA and Production until a consent field exists upstream) to MIT Learn's organization dashboard; it trusts the X-Userinfo header APISIX builds from the mit-learn Keycloak session and confirms org-manager status with a service-authenticated round-trip to MITx Online. `b2b_learner_records` (/api/v1/learner-records) serves identifiable learner, enrollment and course records to contracted partner integrations over Keycloak client-credentials tokens, which the tenant verifies itself against the realm JWKS. Every query reads materialized views that ol-data-platform's dbt builds in the StarRocks `b2b_analytics` and `b2b_learner_records` databases from the dimensional Iceberg layer, which a Dagster schedule rebuilds nightly once enabled (it ships stopped). Tenant isolation is application-layer only: all tenants share one StarRocks pool authenticated as the Vault `app` role. Deployed by ol-infrastructure (applications/ol_analytics_api) to the data EKS clusters, namespace `ol-analytics`, image mitodl/ol-analytics-api-app, min 2 replicas; APISIX hosts analytics.ol.mit.edu (Keycloak redirect flow, dedicated ol-analytics-api-client) and analytics.learn.mit.edu (shares mit-learn's OIDC session, unauth_action pass), with QA at analytics-qa.ol.mit.edu / analytics.rc.learn.mit.edu.

This is a C4 view of **OL Analytics API** within the MIT Open Learning SOA,
focused on **how data is created and propagated** — synchronous request paths
and asynchronous (queued, scheduled, event-driven) flows alike. Use it for
onboarding and as a holistic reference when realigning flows or hunting harmful
cycles and fragile linkages.
